newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen just up next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen just up next week.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to inch up at Monday's primary tender after the finance minister signalled that the next official interest rate move would likely be a cut in several months, dealers said.

They said that after months of rising, yields would now stabilise around present levels because the ministry would not accept much lower prices amid expectations of a rate cut, which analysts said was likely in the third quarter of 1997.

"After (Finance Minister Marek) Belka's statement I do not expect yields to rise much further and a process of yield stabilisation to begin," said Bartlomiej Kumela, fixed income dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
On Thursday, Belka said a real rise in interest rates was presently justified but that he expected rates to be nominally lowered in the second half or in several months time.

Dealers said Monday's 1.2 billion zloty tender would likely be undersubscribed with small interest coming from foreign investors, who were discouraged by likely delays in cutting the zloty's crawling peg devaluation rate.

"Foreign bids could be more speculative on Monday as longer term investors were not keen on Polish paper after Belka said the zloty devaluation rate should not be reduced," one dealer at a Polish bank said.

Belka had said there was no room to cut the crawling peg, now at one percent per month, because such a move would further widen a quickly growing trade gap. This year's budget envisions a nine percent zloty devaluation against the basket in 1997.
Dealers said the minimum price of the benchmark 52-week T-bill would likely remain flat at 82.35, but that the average yield would rise from 21.11 percent at the last auction.
They said the minimum price of the 13-week paper could slip by one or two basis points from 94.95 and the minimum price of the 26-week paper to fall by up to five points from 90.40.

The zloty was expected to drift mainly sideways against the basket next week between 2.8 and 3.1 percent from the trading band centre, with market focus on dollar/mark swings amid small scale foreign investor entry into Polish paper.

"An increasing trade gap will, in the longer-term, depress the zloty but next week the local currency is likely to remain within its recent range around 2.90-2.95 percent from parity," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
The zloty closed the week at 2.96 percent from the parity rate, stronger than last Friday's close at 2.82 percent.
On the money market one-day rates were seen dipping early in the week with some upward potential possible around Thursday as banks pay monthly taxes, dealers said.

They said however, that the scope of the central bank drainages would have the largest impact in establishing one-day rates, which have stabilised around 22.0-22.5 percent after obligatory reserves increased at the end of last month.

"One-day rates could ease in the first part of next week, but tax payments and possible central bank draining operations can pull rates back up later in the week," said Malgorzata Sikora, deposit dealer at ING bank in Warsaw.
